topic: Why the Moon looks bigger near the horizon

candidates.spoken_text: That huge horizon Moon isn't actually bigger.
candidates.visual_concept: giant moon rising behind rooftops, stars
candidates.first_frame_concept: giant moon rising behind rooftops, stars
candidates.payoff_connection: photos show the same width (f1); it is an illusion (f3)

candidates.spoken_text: The rising Moon is actually a bit farther away.
candidates.visual_concept: giant moon over rooftops with a distance arrow from the street
candidates.first_frame_concept: giant moon over rooftops with a distance arrow from the street
candidates.payoff_connection: about 1.5 percent farther at the horizon (f2)

candidates.spoken_text: Hold up a fingernail: does the giant Moon shrink?
candidates.visual_concept: giant moon over rooftops, an index finger rising beside it
candidates.tension: a test the viewer can do
candidates.first_frame_concept: giant moon over rooftops, an index finger rising beside it
candidates.payoff_connection: at arm's length a fingernail covers about the same amount of Moon, low or high (f7)

candidates.spoken_text: Same Moon, two sizes. Which one is real?
candidates.visual_concept: giant low moon beside a small high moon over rooftops
candidates.first_frame_concept: giant low moon beside a small high moon over rooftops
candidates.payoff_connection: same width in photos (f1); the brain makes the difference (f3)

candidates.spoken_text: Your camera says the Moon never grew.
candidates.visual_concept: giant moon over rooftops with a camera pointing at it
candidates.first_frame_concept: giant moon over rooftops with a camera pointing at it
